summary: A specialty-coffee café at 49 Phaya Thai Road, a short walk from BTS Phaya Thai and Airport Rail Link. Worth a detour for signature espresso drinks and a convenient coffee stop between the airport rail link and central Bangkok.
whyGo: The café offers specialty espresso, latte, filter coffee and signature drinks; the Tourism Authority of Thailand also lists non-coffee drinks and pastries.
Its Phaya Thai location is practical for a stop after arriving on the Airport Rail Link or while moving around central Bangkok.
bestFor: Coffee-focused travelers who want to sample a signature drink or ask about available beans.
Travelers connecting through Phaya Thai who want a sit-down break near transit.
skipIf: You need a quiet, reliably quick stop: customer reports describe queues, particularly in the morning.
You need confirmed step-free access or accessible facilities; current official accessibility details were not found.
duration: Allow about 30–60 minutes as a planning estimate; add time if there is a queue.
cost: Budget roughly ฿100–250 per person as a guide, based on Wongnai's listed range; premium or specialty beans may cost more. A recent listed cold brew was ฿160, but check the current menu.
hours: Official location page: daily 8:00 am–4:00 pm, last order 4:00 pm. Recheck before visiting because third-party listings and the Tourism Authority page show different closing times.
bestTime: Try a weekday outside the morning rush for a better chance of a shorter wait. This is a practical suggestion; no official crowd forecast is published.
gettingThere: Go to 49 Phaya Thai Road, Ratchathewi. The Tourism Authority of Thailand says BTS Phaya Thai is about a 1–2 minute walk away; the station also connects with the Airport Rail Link. Confirm the exact pedestrian exit and route in a map app on the day.
booking: No reservation process was listed on the official location page. Plan to order on arrival; call +66 80 958 8050 to check queues, current menu or any group arrangements.
accessibility: The venue's official page gives an address and transit information but no step-free access, doorway, seating or restroom details. Contact the café before visiting if these affect your plans.
practicalTips: Check the official location page on the day: its current hours are 8:00 am–4:00 pm, while the Tourism Authority listing still says 8:00 am–5:00 pm.
Ask staff which signature drinks and beans are available that day; menus and seasonal lots can change.
Wongnai reviews report queues, so avoid scheduling this as a tight connection stop.
decemberNotes: No December-specific event or holiday schedule was found. December is a busy travel period in Bangkok; allow extra time around Phaya Thai transit and verify opening hours directly, especially near public holidays.
uncertainties: Official and Tourism Authority opening times conflict; the venue's own location page currently gives 8:00 am–4:00 pm.
Current item-by-item menu prices, queue patterns and holiday hours may change before December 2026.
Accessibility details and whether reservations are accepted are not published on the official location page.
